subject.title: memory_search: chokidar file watcher silently stops delivering events, index goes stale

question: Should unconfigured `memorySearch.sync.intervalMinutes` become a default periodic fallback, or should periodic memory sync remain opt-in with docs or doctor guidance?
rationale: The bug needs a recovery path when watcher events are missed, but changing the default from disabled to periodic background work affects upgrade behavior, resource usage, and possible embedding-provider calls.

options.title: Accept a scoped default fallback
options.body: After the linked PR scopes dirty marking correctly, merge a non-zero default fallback such as 30 minutes with explicit `0` opt-out and upgrade proof.

options.title: Keep periodic sync opt-in
options.body: Preserve the `0` default, document `intervalMinutes` as the workaround, and consider doctor guidance for users who hit watcher outages.

options.title: Defer to broader watcher health work
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose a heartbeat or watcher-health design instead of relying on a periodic rescan fallback.

recommendation.title: Accept a scoped default fallback
recommendation.body: After the linked PR scopes dirty marking correctly, merge a non-zero default fallback such as 30 minutes with explicit `0` opt-out and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory index and stale reindex safety work makes this the strongest routing candidate for the memory correctness/default tradeoff.
